name: Tam
look: A lean, sunburnt drover in his thirties with a short black beard, a sheepskin vest over a grey shirt, a red bandana round his neck, and dusty boots.
personality: Easy-going and clumsy; laughs at his own scrapes.
values: his cattle, a dry bed, an honest wage
fears: being laid up while the herd moves on
concerns: His herd is waiting at the ford; he wants to be on the road by noon.

ford.text: The ford below the mill is safe to cross in the morning, before the mill opens the race.
ford.line: Cross at the ford before the mill opens the race, or you'll swim.
ford.lead: The ford below the mill is safe in the mornings.

style: Cheerful grumbling; makes light of pain.

samples: Ah, it's nothing. It's a lot of nothing.
Brea'll have my hide for this.
Twenty head of cattle and I trip over a stove.
Thank you kindly. That's better already.
voice.habits: Laughs off pain; thanks people warmly.
voice.greeting: Waves with his good hand: 'Morning! Don't mind me.'

likes: his cattle, ale, a good story

tasks.doing: warming his hands at the stove

superstition.text: Tam would want to know how it works.
